To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the protein corona formed onto circulating liposomes, when injected in vivo, could be deemed as valuable tool of the proteome to discover novel biomarkers for cancer diagnostics.

1) the blood circulating NP protein corona can be exploited as a tool for the comprehensive analysis of the blood circulation proteomics; 2) the NP (liposome) protein corona can capture and amplify low molecular-weight and low-abundant tumor-specific proteins, that cannot be detected by plasma proteomics, performed in comparison.

the protein corona formed onto blood-circulating nanoparticles is an excellent tool to discover new biomarkers in experimental disease models, and that this tool can be exploited in a variety of disease models, as well as in clinical studies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel approach for the identification of cancer biomarkers, based on the use of blood circulating nanoparticles as a scavengng tool.
the development of an in vivo protein capture tool based on lipid-based nanoparticles (liposomes) to facilitate the discovery and validation of cancer biomarkers in the blood proteome.

the development of a novel technology to identify novel cancer biomarkers in the blood circulation, based on the use of circulating nanoparticles (NPs), which are capable of capturing and amplifying the concentration of tumor-specific proteins, which are otherwise present at very low concentrations in the blood.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the blood-circulating NPs are able to capture and amplify the low molecular weight and low abundant tumor biomarker proteins that are released by the tumor cells into the bloodstream and are not detectable by plasma proteome analysis, performed in a parallel fashion.
the in vivo nanoparticle protein corona is a valuable tool of plasma proteome in experimental animal disease models to discover potential biomarkers.
this is a very interesting study that provides a new approach for the identification of potential biomarkers in the blood of cancer patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel scavenging tool based on the blood-circulating NP protein corona, for the discovery of novel biomarker candidates.

the blood-circulating NPs could be considered as a valuable tool for biomarker discovery, by facilitating the identification of low MW proteins, that are released from the growing tumor and are not detectable in the bulk of plasma.
the protein corona that spontaneously forms on blood-circulating NPs can be used to discover novel biomarker molecules in the blood of tumor-bearing mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the in vivo protein corona formed onto blood-circulating nanoparticles could be deemed as an effective and valuable tool of the plasma proteome to allow the discovery and identification of potential biomarkers for cancer diagnostics.
the blood-circulating NP corona can serve as a novel tool of the blood circulation proteomic space to discover novel cancer biomarkers.
blood-circulating NPs can be exploited as a tool to discover novel biomarkers for cancer diagnostics.
